BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r13.claim: Guidance means teaching Pharaoh to know his Lord and fear His wrath and punishment with reverence.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r13.anchor: Ve seni Rabbine hidâyet edeyim Rabbini tanımaya irşad edeyim {فَتَخْشَىٰ} de haşyetlenesin O’nun gazabından, ikābından korkup O’na tâzim ile saygı duyasın.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r14.claim: The learned fear God; those who lack knowledge lack reverence, are not guarded, and fall into wrongdoing.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r14.anchor: Çünkü إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا۟’dır [Fâtır 35/28]. Bilmeyenlerin saygısı olmaz.

ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r15.claim: These verses unpack the gentle address Moses was commanded to use in Ṭā Hā 20:44.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#2/r15.anchor: Bu iki âyette Sûre-i Tâhâ’da geçen فَقُولَا لَهُۥ قَوْلًۭا لَّيِّنًۭا لَعَلَّهُۥ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَىٰ [20/44] âyetinin bir nevi tafsîli ile “kavl-i leyyin”i bir îzah vardır.

QASHANI:79:18-26/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:18-26/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:18-26/r1.claim: Purification means annihilating selfhood; guidance to fear is knowledge of the unity of the Essence, which softens and dissolves selfhood.
QASHANI:79:18-26/r1.anchor: هل لك إلى أن تزكى } بالفناء عن أنائيتك { وأهديك إلى } الوحدة الذاتية بالمعرفة الحقيقية { فتخشى }

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r21.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r21.claim: Knowledge follows guidance and reverent fear follows knowledge, as supported by 35:28.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p432#2/r21.anchor: والعلم تابع للهدى والخشية تابعة للعلم، إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء [فاطر: 28]

JISHUMI:v10p7268/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r7.claim: Zakāh is growth in good; a zākī is one growing in good, and tazakkī is seeking to become zākī.
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r7.anchor: والزكاة: النمو في الخير، والزاكي: النامي في الخير، والتزكي: طلب الطالب أن يصير زاكيا

JISHUMI:v10p7268/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r8.claim: Khashya and khawf mean the same thing: fear.
JISHUMI:v10p7268/r8.anchor: والخشية والخوف بمعنى، خشي يخشى خشية

JISHUMI:v10p7271/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r5.claim: The verse shows that guidance is an indication and a path to knowing God, rather than faith itself.
JISHUMI:v10p7271/r5.anchor: يدل قوله تعالى: (وأهديك) أن الهداية هي الدلالة، والطريق إلى معرفة الله تعالى، لا نفس الإيمان

MUQATIL:79:15-26/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r7.claim: Being guided to the Lord means being guided to His greatness, so that one fears Him.
MUQATIL:79:15-26/r7.anchor: { وأهديك إلى ربك } إلى عظمته { فتخشى }

NAHHAS:v5p143/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p143/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p143/r10.claim: فتخشى is coordinated with what precedes and means fearing God's punishment by avoiding disobedience.
NAHHAS:v5p143/r10.anchor: عطف وكذا ( فتخشى ) أي فتخشى عقابه بترك معاصيه

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r4.claim: Moses was told to invite Pharaoh peacefully to follow God's Revelation first, just as the Prophet invited Quraysh, in keeping with the instruction to speak gently.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r4.anchor: Moses was instructed to first invite Pharaoh to follow God’s Revelation, as in 20:44: Yet speak unto him gently

STUDYQURAN:79:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r5.claim: The Quran teaches that a community is not punished for wrongdoing before receiving guidance through a messenger.
STUDYQURAN:79:15/r5.anchor: It is a common Quranic theme that no community is punished for wrongdoing until it has been offered guidance, as indicated in 28:59:

TABRISI:79:15-24/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r2.speaker: أهل الحجاز وعباس ويعقوب
TABRISI:79:15-24/r2.claim: These readers recite tazakka with a doubled z; the other readers use the lighter form.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r2.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز وعباس ويعقوب تزكى بتشديد الزاء والباقون بتخفيفها

TABRISI:79:15-24/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r6.claim: Tazakka means purifying oneself from unbelief; an omitted noun is understood, as in asking whether the addressee has a wish or need for it.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r6.anchor: { تزكى } معناه تطهر من الكفر والمبتدأ محذوف من اللفظ مراد في المعنى

TABRISI:79:15-24/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r7.claim: The light form is understood as tatazakka with its initial ta deleted; the doubled reading assimilates that ta into z because the sounds are close.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r7.anchor: ومن قال تزكى أراد تتزكى فأدغم تاء التفعل في الزاء لتقاربهما ومن خفف حذف التاء

TABRISI:79:15-24/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r13.claim: Guiding Pharaoh to his Lord can mean teaching him to know his Creator and Sustainer, or guiding him to the path of God's approval and reward.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r13.anchor: { وأهديك إلى ربك } أي وأدلك إلى معرفة ربك وأنه خلقك ورباك

TABRISI:79:15-24/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:15-24/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:15-24/r14.claim: The result of that guidance is fear of God and leaving what He prohibited; the narrative omits the step that Moses went to Pharaoh and called him.
TABRISI:79:15-24/r14.anchor: { فتخشى } أي فتخافه فتفارق ما نهاك عنه وفي الكلام حذف تقديره فأتاه ودعاه

RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r1.speaker: القائلون بأن معرفة الله لا تستفاد إلا من الهادي
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r1.claim: Those who make a guide indispensable for knowing God cite this phrase as explicit proof that knowledge of God comes through a guide.
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r1.anchor: القائلون بأن معرفة الله لا تستفاد إلا من الهادي تمسكوا بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r2.speaker: القائلون بأن معرفة الله لا تستفاد إلا من الهادي
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r2.claim: They argue that purification already covers all necessary duties, so restating guidance shows that guidance to God is the mission's chief aim.
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r2.anchor: يتناول جميع الأمور التي لا بد للمبعوث إليه منها ، فيدخل فيه هذه الهداية

RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r3.speaker: القائلون بأن معرفة الله لا تستفاد إلا من الهادي
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r3.claim: They also argue that Moses concludes his address with guidance, signaling that it is the mission's noblest objective.
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r3.anchor: أن موسى ختم كلامه عليه ، وذلك ينبه أيضا على أنه أشرف المقاصد من البعثة

RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r4.claim: Rāzī accepts that instruction and indication can help disclose truth, but rejects the claim that knowledge is impossible without a teacher.
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r4.anchor: لا نمنع أن يكون للتنبيه والإشارة معونة في الكشف عن الحق

RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r5.claim: Knowledge of God precedes obedience: the verse mentions guidance before fear and makes fear follow from it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r5.anchor: دلت الآية على أن معرفة الله مقدمة على طاعته ، لأنه ذكر الهداية وجعل الخشية مؤخرة عنها

RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r6.claim: Fear of God depends on knowing Him; those who know God fear Him, and fear is the source of good while feeling safe invites evil.
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r6.anchor: دلت الآية على أن الخشية لا تكون إلا بالمعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r7.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r7.claim: A Prophetic saying compares the God-fearing traveler who sets out at night and reaches his destination with the one who fears God and attains good.
RAZI-FULL:v31p37#2/r7.anchor: من خاف أدلج ، ومن أدلج بلغ المنزل

TABATABAI:79:15-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r1.claim: The account of Moses and Pharaoh warns polytheists who deny resurrection and use that denial against religious law, consoles the Prophet over rejection, and threatens his opponents.
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r1.anchor: وفيها عظة وإنذار للمشركين المنكرين للبعث وقد توسلوا به إلى رد الدعوة الدينية إذ لا معنى لتشريع الدين لولا المعاد

TABATABAI:79:15-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r2.claim: The destruction of Pharaoh and his army proves Moses' divinely authorized mission; such a mission entails God's lordship over people, contrary to the polytheists' claim that lesser lords govern them.
TABATABAI:79:15-19/r2.anchor: ولا تتم رسالته من جانبه تعالى إلا بربوبية منه تعالى للناس

TABATABAI:79:19-22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī links fear of God with knowledge and cites the statement that God's learned servants fear Him.
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r1.anchor: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء

TABATABAI:79:19-22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r2.claim: One reading takes tazakkā as repentance from tyranny and return to God; the ensuing fear is faith-driven fear that motivates obedience and restrains sin.
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r2.anchor: الخشية الملازمة للإيمان الداعية إلى الطاعة والرادعة عن المعصية

TABATABAI:79:19-22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r3.claim: If purification means obedience and avoidance of sin, “I will guide you to your Lord, so you will fear” explains that purification by apposition.
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r3.anchor: كان قوله { وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى } مفسرا لما قبله والعطف عطف تفسير

TABATABAI:79:19-22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r4.claim: The fear that follows guidance accords with the statement that God's servants who truly fear Him are the learned.
TABATABAI:79:19-22/r4.anchor: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء

BURSEVI:v10p249/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249/r8.claim: An omitted genitive complement is understood: Moses will guide Pharaoh to knowledge of his Lord.
BURSEVI:v10p249/r8.anchor: وأهديك إلى ربك} وأرشدك إلى معرفته

BURSEVI:v10p249/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249/r9.claim: Purification comes before adornment: fear follows knowledge of God, and knowing God makes fear the goal of guidance.

BURSEVI:v10p249/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249/r10.claim: A report says that when God indicated Pharaoh would not purify himself, Moses asked why he should go; God ordered him to proceed, since twelve thousand angels in heaven seek knowledge of destiny without attaining it.
BURSEVI:v10p249/r10.anchor: فقال موسى فكيف أمضي إليه وقد علمت إنه لن يفعل

BURSEVI:v10p249/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249/r11.claim: Fear is the essential outcome of guidance: whoever fears God does every good, while whoever feels secure dares every evil.
BURSEVI:v10p249/r11.anchor: وجعل الخشية غاية للهداية لأنها ملاك الأمر لأن من خشى الله أتى منه كل خير

BURSEVI:v10p249/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r12.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p249/r12.claim: The Prophet’s saying that whoever fears sets out at night and whoever sets out reaches the destination illustrates fear’s role in attaining the goal.
BURSEVI:v10p249/r12.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : من خاف أدلج ومن أدلج بلغ المنزل

BURSEVI:v10p249/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249/r13.claim: God told Moses to approach Pharaoh with an invitational question so tactful speech might draw him gently from obstinacy.
BURSEVI:v10p249/r13.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى أمر موسى عليه السلام ، بأن يخاطبه بالاستفهام الذي معناه العرض

BURSEVI:v10p249/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p249/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p249/r14.claim: This unthreatening, detailed offer explains the instruction to speak gently in 20:44: it states neither polytheism, ignorance, nor disbelief, but what purification entails and where guidance leads.
BURSEVI:v10p249/r14.anchor: فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil say Moses offers to call Pharaoh to worship his Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬8)، ومقاتل (¬9): وأدعوك إلى عبادة ربك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r2.claim: The gloss says Pharaoh would be saved through fear of God and affirm God’s oneness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r2.anchor: {فتخشى} فتسلم من خشية الله، وتوحد الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r3.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r3.claim: The scholars of meaning say it is fear of God’s punishment, fulfilled by carrying out the duties imposed out of that fear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p187/r3.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: فتخشى عقابه، ويكون المعنى: تؤدي ما

QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r4.claim: Moses offers to establish the truth of his message through signs and make Pharaoh know the truth of the religion, asking whether he wants this guidance.
QUSHAYRI:v3p389/r4.anchor: أقرر لك بالآيات صحة ما أقول ، وأعرفك صحة الدين . . فهل لك ذلك ؟

SULAMI:v2p370#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p370#4/r1.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
SULAMI:v2p370#4/r1.claim: Fear of God is the fruit of sound guidance, as the verse makes clear.
SULAMI:v2p370#4/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن علي الترمذي : الخشية ميراث صحة الهداية الا ترى الله يقول : ﴿ وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى

ASAD-NOTES:79:15#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:15#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:15#n8/r1.claim: Asad says that without full awareness of God, a person cannot distinguish what is morally right from wrong.
ASAD-NOTES:79:15#n8/r1.anchor: so long as man is not fully aware of the existence of God, he cannot really discern between what is morally right or wrong

ASAD-NOTES:79:15#n8/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:15#n8/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:15#n8/r2.claim: Because God is just, Asad says He does not punish people before they attain moral discernment, linking this principle to 6:31.
ASAD-NOTES:79:15#n8/r2.anchor: since God is just, He does not punish anyone who has not yet attained to such a discernment

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r1.claim: Quran attributes fear of God to messengers who convey His messages, followers of the Reminder, believers, scholars, and those God approves and who are content with Him.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r1.anchor: وتسند خشية الله في القرآن إلى: الذين يبلغون رسالات ربهم، ومن اتبع الذكر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r2.claim: Attributing fear to mountains and stones animates lifeless matter, depicting it as able to perceive, respond, fear God, and humble itself.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r2.anchor: فإذا كانت خشية الله متوقَّعة من الجبل كما في آية الحشر، أو من الحجارة كما في آية البقرة:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r3.claim: Humility is an act of the heart; a humble voice, face, or gaze reflects the heart's own humility.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r3.anchor: وإذا خشع الصوت أو خشع الوجه أو البصر، فإنما يكون ذلك من خشوع القلب.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r4.claim: Quranic khushu is consistently directed to God and describes the believers' state in this worldly life.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p227/r4.anchor: فكل خشوع في القآن إنها هو لله تعالى: يأتي وصفا أو بيانا لحال المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r4.claim: The promised purification is guidance to God’s oneness and knowledge; خشية means fear, which arises from knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r4.anchor: هذا تفسير للتزكية، وهي الهداية إلى توحيد الله تعالى ومعرفته، فتخشى: أي تخافه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r5.claim: Fear is named because it is the core of the matter.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r6.claim: An omitted narrative says Moses delivered the commanded message, then performed a miracle proving his truthfulness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p398/r6.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف، أي فذهب وقال له ما أمره به ربه، وأتبع ذلك بالمعجزة الدالة على صدقه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r1.claim: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to knowledge of God; fear follows knowledge, since only those who know God truly fear Him, and fear is the foundation of good action.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r1.anchor: أي أرشدك إلى معرفته عز وجل فتعرفه فتخشى إذا الخشية لا تكون إلا بعد معرفته

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r2.speaker: الترمذي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r2.claim: A hadith from Abū Hurayra says that whoever fears God sets out at night, and whoever sets out reaches the destination.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r2.anchor: ومنه قوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فيما رواه الترمذي عن أبي هريرة من خاف أدلج ومن أدلج بلغ المنزل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r3.claim: The question gently invites Pharaoh and draws him down from arrogance; purification precedes guidance as cleansing before adornment, and the invitation elaborates the command to speak gently.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p29#4/r3.anchor: وفي الاستفهام ما لا يخفى من التلطف في الدعوة والأستنزال عن العتو وهذا ضرب تفصيل لقوله تعالى فقولا له قولا لينا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r10.claim: Moses would call Pharaoh to worship and affirm God's oneness so that he would fear God's punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p328/r10.anchor: أي: أدعوك إلى عبادة ربك وتوحيده فتخشى عقابه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r5.claim: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to know God, so that he will fear Him by doing duties and leaving prohibitions; fear follows knowledge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r5.anchor: { فتخشى } بأداء الواجبات وترك المحرمات، إذ الخشية إنما تكون بعد المعرفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:17-22/r6.claim: This offer to speak gently spells out the instruction to use gentle words with Pharaoh.

BINTSHATI:v1p144/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r1.claim: The invitation echoes the command to Moses and Aaron in Ṭā Hā, including the instruction to speak gently and the hope that Pharaoh might remember or fear.
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r1.anchor: فقولا له قولاً ليناً لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

BINTSHATI:v1p144/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r4.claim: Guidance is direction to the straight path; the root is associated with a raised rock in water that prevents stumbling and with daylight that makes the path clear.
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r4.anchor: والهداية: الإرشاد إلى الطريق المستقيم، ولعل أصل استعماله في الهدى: الصخرة الناتئة في الماء

BINTSHATI:v1p144/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r5.claim: Calling God “your Lord” to a Pharaoh who denied Moses' Lord is intended to establish the claim and prepare for “then you will fear”: such fear requires faith in his Lord.
BINTSHATI:v1p144/r5.anchor: واللافت هنا إضافة رب إلى كاف الخطاب، مع أن فرعون لم يكن يؤمن برب موسى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r14.claim: After purification from associating partners with God, Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to his Lord, the creator, benefactor, and nurturer who teaches pleasing actions and blameworthy traits; this develops the gentle call in Ta Ha.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r14.anchor: أي أبين لك بعد التزكية بالإيمان الذي هو الأساس : كيف المسير { إلى ربك } أي الموجد لك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r15.claim: Guidance should lead Pharaoh to act in fear: perform obligations and avoid prohibitions, completing purification. Fear motivates all good, while feeling secure encourages evil.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p313/r15.anchor: أي فيتسبب عن ذلك أنك تصير تعمل أعمال من يخاف من عذابه خوفا عظيما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r6.claim: Moses' wording offers and encourages Pharaoh to accept guidance, fulfilling the instruction to speak gently in 20:44.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p75/r6.anchor: و { هل لك إلى أن تزكى وأهديك إلى ربك } عرض وترغيب قال تعالى : { فقولا له قولا لينا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r3.claim: If Pharaoh is ready for purification, Moses' guidance will lead him to fear; the order of the clauses follows the order of events, though waw can convey that sequence contextually.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r3.anchor: ولذلك أعقبه بعطف { وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى } أي إن كان فيك إعداد نفسك للتزكية يكن إرشادي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r4.claim: Guidance is pointing along a path to the desired goal, provided the person guided accepts it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r4.anchor: والهداية الدلالة علء الطريق الموصل إلى المطلوب إذا قبلها المهدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r5.claim: Making fear follow guidance indicates that true fear of God depends on knowledge of Him, as stated in 35:28.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r5.anchor: وتفريع { فتخشى } على { أهديك } إشارة إلى أن خشية الله لا تكون إلا بالمعرفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r6.speaker: الواسطي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r6.claim: Al-Wasiti describes successive stages: beginnings of knowledge are fear, then reverence, glorification, awe, and finally annihilation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r6.anchor: قال الطيبي : وعن الواسطي : أوائل العلم الخشية ، ثم الإجلال ، ثم التعظيم ، ثم الهيبة ، ثم الفناء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r7.claim: Mentioning only fear is concise and eloquent because fear is the foundation of every good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r7.anchor: وفي الاقتصار على ذكر الخشية إيجاز بليغ لأن الخشية ملاك كل خير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r8.claim: In al-Tirmidhi's Jami, Abu Hurayra says he heard the Prophet teach that one who sets out early from fear reaches the destination; Ibn Ashur gives no grading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r8.anchor: وفي ( جامع الترمذي ) عن أبي هريرة قال : ( سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من خاف أدلج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r9.claim: Calling God your Lord gently invites Pharaoh toward monotheism without provoking him: the familiar title could secure a hearing, allowing faith to enter gradually after he hears Moses' proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p77/r9.anchor: وذكر له الإلاه الحق بوصف { ربك } دون أن يذكر له اسم الله العلم أو غيره من طرق التعريف إلطافا في الدعوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r1.claim: Khashya means fear and, in religious usage, specifically fear of God; its verb is treated as intransitive because the understood object is God, as with believing in God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p78/r1.anchor: والخشية : الخوف فإذا أطلقت في لسان الشرع يراد بها خشية الله تعالى ، ولهذا نزل فعلها هنا منزلة اللازم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#4/r1.claim: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to God's oneness and worship so that he will fear God's punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p20#4/r1.anchor: وأهديك إلى ربك أي أدعوك إلى توحيده وعبادته فتخشى عذابه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r1.claim: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to knowledge of God by recounting His attributes, so Pharaoh may know Him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r1.anchor: وأرشدك إلى معرفة الله بذكر صفاته فتعرفه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r2.claim: Fear of God only comes through knowledge of Him, as the Qur'an says that those who fear God among His servants are the learned.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r2.anchor: لأن الخشية لا تكون إلا بالمعرفة قال الله تعالى إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r3.speaker: بعض الحكماء
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r3.claim: A sage says that whoever knows God cannot disobey Him even for an instant.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r3.anchor: وعن بعض الحكماء اعرف الله فمن عرف الله لم يقدر أن يعصيه طرفة عين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r4.claim: Fear is the basis of conduct: fearing God brings every good, while feeling secure leads one to dare every evil.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r4.anchor: فالخشية ملاك الأمر من خشى الله أتى منه كل خير ومن أمن من اجترأ على كل شر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r5.claim: A hadith says that whoever fears sets out by night, and whoever sets out by night reaches his destination.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r5.anchor: ومنه لحديث من خاف أدلج ومن أدلج بلغ المنزل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r6.claim: Moses begins with an interrogative invitation, like a host gently asking a guest to stay.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r6.anchor: بدأ مخاطبته بالاستفهام الذى معناه العرض كما يقول الرجل لضيفه هل لك أن تنزل بنا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r7.claim: He follows with gentle speech to attract Pharaoh kindly and coax him away from arrogance, in keeping with the command to speak softly to him.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p314#10/r7.anchor: واردفه الكلام الرقيق ليستدعيه باللطف فى القول ويستنزله بالمداراة عن عتوة كما أمر بذلك فى قوله تعالى فقولا له قولا لينا

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r14.claim: Moses offers guidance to obey the Lord, so Pharaoh will fear and heed Him.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18.speaker: صخر بن جويرية
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18.claim: Sakhr ibn Juwayriyya reports Moses asking how to approach Pharaoh when he knew he would refuse; God ordered him to go and said twelve thousand angels seek knowledge of the decree without attaining it.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:15-20/r18.anchor: قال صخر بن جويرية: لما بعث الله موسى إلى فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p73/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p73/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p73/r3.claim: The Moses story interrupts the argument from the single blast to the proof in 79:27 because Pharaoh’s tyranny parallels the polytheists’ defiance, while Moses’ mission parallels the Prophet’s; it comforts the Prophet and warns Quraysh leaders and polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p73/r3.anchor: هذه الآية اعتراض بين جملة { فإنما هي زجرة واحدة } ( النازعات : 13 ) وبين جملة { أأنتم أشد خلقا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p73/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p73/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p73/r4.claim: “Has the story reached you?” is meant to kindle interest, not test prior knowledge; it expects no answer and introduces the detailed story as important news.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p73/r4.anchor: و { هل أتاك } استفهام صوري يقصد من أمثاله تشويق السامع إلى الخير من غير قصد إلى استعلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r1.claim: The story alludes to Quraysh leaders such as Abu Jahl as Pharaoh and to the masses as Pharaoh’s assembled people; Muslims accordingly called Abu Jahl “the Pharaoh of this community.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r1.anchor: وفي القصة كلها تعريض بسادة قريش من أهل الكفر مثل أبي جهل بتنظيرهم بفرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r2.claim: The emphatic inna and initial lām treat the story’s listeners as deniers of its lessons because they do not act on its admonitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r2.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر ب { إن } ولام الابتداء لتنزيل السامعين الذين سيقت لهم القصة منزلة من ينكر ما فيها من المواعظ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r8.claim: Moses offers to guide Pharaoh to worship his Lord.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r8.anchor: {وأهديك إلى ربك} أي: أدلك إلى عبادة ربك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r9.claim: The guidance would make Pharaoh humble, obedient, and fearful instead of hard and corrupt.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p315/r9.anchor: {فتخشى} أي: فيصير قلبك خاضعا له مطيعا خاشيا بعدما كان قاسيا خبيثا بعيدا من الخير.

TAB-FULL:v24p81#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p81#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p81#2/r1.claim: Moses is told to invite Pharaoh to guidance to what pleases his Lord—the true religion—so that he fears God's punishment by fulfilling obligations and avoiding prohibitions.
TAB-FULL:v24p81#2/r1.anchor: ما ألزمك من فرائضه، واجتناب ما نهاك عنه من معاصيه
